nodes.summary: The family of all intervals $(l, u] \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ with real endpoints $l < u$. It is used as a generating π-system for the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Nonempty bounded half-open intervals

nodes.summary: Let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be finite measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $\mu_1((a, b]) = \mu_2((a, b])$ for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, where $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$, then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.
nodes.title: Rectangle uniqueness for measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: Let $F : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$, and let $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ be measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. Suppose that for all $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $a_i \le b_i$ for every $i$, both $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ assign the rectangle $(a, b] = \prod_{i=1}^d (a_i, b_i]$ the mass $\max(\Delta_{a,b} F, 0)$, where $\Delta_{a,b} F$ is the rectangle value of $F$ at $a, b$. Then $\mu_1 = \mu_2$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness from rectangle values

nodes.summary:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$. If $\mu(\{x : x \le a\}) = 
u(\{x : x \le a\})$ for every $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$, where $x \le a$ means $x_i \le a_i$ for every $i$, then $\mu = 
u$.
nodes.title: Quadrant uniqueness for measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: The Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$ is the σ-algebra generated by the nonempty bounded half-open intervals $(l, u]$ with $l < u$.
nodes.title: Half-open intervals generate the Borel σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}$

nodes.summary: The product σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Borel σ-algebra on each coordinate, is generated by the boxes $\prod_{i=1}^d (-\infty, a_i]$ for $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: Lower orthants generate the product σ-algebra on $\mathbb{R}^d$

nodes.summary: There is a sequence of nonempty bounded half-open intervals $(l, u]$ with $l < u$ whose union is $\mathbb{R}$; for example, the intervals $(-n - 1, n + 1]$ for $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
nodes.title: Half-open intervals countably span $\mathbb{R}$

nodes.summary: If two intervals $(l, u]$ and $(l', u']$ in $\mathbb{R}$ with $l < u$ and $l' < u'$ intersect, then their intersection is again an interval $(l'', u'']$ with $l'' < u''$.
nodes.title: Nonempty bounded half-open intervals form a π-system

nodes.summary: For $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ let $L_a = \prod_{i=1}^d (-\infty, a_i]$. If two such boxes $L_a$ and $L_b$ intersect, then their intersection is $L_c$ for some $c \in \mathbb{R}^d$.
nodes.title: Lower orthants form a π-system

nodes.title: Rectangle value of a function

nodes.summary: Let $d$ be a natural number, let $a, b \in \mathbb{R}^d$, and let $S$ be a finite set of coordinate indices in $\{0, \dots, d-1\}$. The vertex of the rectangle $(a, b]$ selected by $S$ is the point $v \in \mathbb{R}^d$ with $v_i = a_i$ for $i \in S$ and $v_i = b_i$ for $i \notin S$.
nodes.title: Vertex of a rectangle

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved

inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
